_comment: Build classifiers as data. Global product config, never per-deck (design 13.4): one rule set,
one version, every deck. Hand-editable today; a panel is a later, small addition because the
values already live here behind an evaluator (design 13.7).
SCOPE OF THIS FILE, and the boundary is blast radius, not technical possibility (design 13.3):
build classifiers ONLY. Each has exactly one consumer -- its own category count. The derive
parsers stay code (they emit typed schema fields that many gates read), and segment.ts is
frozen forever because it runs above the paid layer and decides what was bought.
Every pattern is matched case-insensitively against oracle text. Editing one moves every deck,
so the gate is build-population.ts over the 71 calibration decks -- nothing else in the repo
can see build categories at all.

_answerClasses: The doctrine (design 12.3): every deck should carry creature, artifact and enchantment removal,
graveyard hate, and some land interaction. `permanent` is not a class -- a card that answers
any permanent answers all of them, so it expands.

rules.why: Only utility lands fill a land ROLE, so a basic never reads as double duty. The build LAND COUNT is separate -- computeBuild counts every land copy itself.

A land that sacrifices itself for TWO+ lands nets +1 mana. A fetchland gets one (net 0), which is fixing, not ramp. DERIVED (#1266; it was a printed-text pattern): a land with a `fetch` mana line whose fixed amount is 2 or more.

2+ mana from a bare {T} is a net extra mana per land drop -- unless it enters tapped, which makes it unusable the turn it lands. DERIVED (#1266; it was two printed-text patterns): an `activated` mana line whose cost is exactly {T} and whose fixed amount is 2 or more, on a land the shared land classifier (`classifyLand`) does not read as entering tapped (`unconditional` or `unclassified`). A GATED line counts (owner ruling 2026-10-13, #1169: a gated mana source is still a mana source, conditioned on the deck): Urza's Tower, Muraganda Raceway.

Lands with activated/channel removal (Eiganjo) fill the removal role; graveyard-exile lands (Bojuka Bog) do not, because their exile derives `fromZone: graveyard` and no removal clause accepts that (the printed `graveyardHate` guard was deleted, #1326). Damage counts when its target can be a permanent (#1294, owner ruling 2026-10-22: Sunscorched Desert, "target player or planeswalker", at any amount; `reachesPermanent`), replacing the printed `damageRemoval`; the answer classes keep their own 2+ rule for "any target".

A DERIVED MANA LINE that adds mana (#1190; it read the ability list's mana-generation kind): a tap, a trigger (Birgi), a sacrifice outlet (Phyrexian Altar), a grant, an Aura's trigger, a ritual. A mana-generation LABEL with no line behind it (Honest Work, Imprisoned in the Moon, Mark of Sakiko, Utopia Vow: owner 2026-10-13, an Aura counts only if mana is its purpose) is none. RAMP IS A NET GAIN (owner's rule, roadmap I4): Dark Ritual is {B} for {B}{B}{B} and Manamorphose is two mana for two mana plus a cantrip. The net test judges ONE-SHOTS ONLY, from the line's own net -- a permanent mana source repeats, so a dork nets 0 the turn it lands and is ramp anyway.

YOUR DRAW, OR EVERYONE'S (#977): Baleful Mastery's "an opponent draws a card" is the opponent's card, not yours, and it sat on Gisa's Draw shelf. A symmetric draw (Howling Mine, control any) still draws you a card and stays.

A DRAW THAT COMES BACK (owner, 2026-09-05): ten Rhystic Studies are not ten Divinations, and the count said they were. Anything above `once` on the SAME ability; per-cycle ({T}: draw, once a round) counts as an engine by the owner's ruling. Measured on the 71 decks before this rule: 400 engine cards, 470 one-shots, 104 unlabelled.

A draw `repeats.ts` REFUSED to label, on a card with no labelled engine draw beside it. Shown, not hidden: unlabelled beats mislabelled, and a reader who sees 3 unlabelled knows the engine count is a floor.

CARDS PUT FROM YOUR LIBRARY INTO YOUR HAND ARE CARD ADVANTAGE, NOT DRAW (owner 2026-10-22, #1302; CR 121.5: drawing is its own instruction, so a draw payoff does not see Fact or Fiction, Dark Confidant or Ad Nauseam). A new leaf in Card advantage beside draw, card selection, impulse draw and tutor. This reverses the 2026-10-02 'fact or fiction is a draw spell' line the printed `digToHand` pattern (`draw.dig`) stood on. DERIVED (derive 384): the `to-hand` effect kind and its `amount`. Included: a pile (Fact or Fiction), two or three of a look (Dig Through Time), every card of a type (Tamiyo, Winding Way), a reveal that turns up one card (Dark Confidant, Ad Nauseam, Coiling Oracle's hand branch). A reveal-until-a-NAMED-card (Demonic Consultation, Divining Witch, Spoils of the Vault) is a tutor (owner 2026-10-22, `Ability.named`); a swap or a draw replacement (Scroll Rack, Abundance, Underrealm Lich) nets zero cards and is card selection (`Ability.netZero`); an opponent's pick (Karn, Scion of Urza) is not YOUR choice, so it stays here. NOT the Impulse line (owner 2026-10-02, still binding): one card chosen from a larger look stays card selection; a card with that line AND a conditional bigger branch (See the Truth, Accumulate Wisdom, Flow State) keeps its base case. A typed dig ("a creature card from among them") reaches here through `handFill.dig`.

A TYPED DIG IS CARDS TO HAND TOO (owner 2026-10-22: "take a Wizard from the top 4 is better the more Wizards you run"). "Look at the top four cards, you may reveal an Elemental, Island, or Mountain card and put it into your hand", "if it's a Zombie card, you may reveal it and put it into your hand", "reveal cards until you reveal a creature card" keep their `search` kind for the tutor EDGES (a Zombie dig is worth more with Zombies) and carry `Ability.toHand` (derive 385): the same hand-fill as `handFill.effect`, so the two cannot drift. NOT a printed search of your library (Demonic Tutor: `librarySearch`, a tutor, no `toHand`). The same refusals as `handFill.effect`: one card YOU pick from a larger look is the Impulse line (card selection), a reveal-until-a-named-card is a tutor, a draw replacement or swap is card selection.

A MANA SOURCE THAT COMES BACK (owner, 2026-09-05: 'do the same for ramp'). A rock or a dork taps every round, a Treasure ENGINE makes one every turn (a line that makes a mana TOKEN: #1190 read any token-generation ability, so a creature-token engine was a mana engine), and a ramp land is itself the source; a ritual or a one-off pair of Treasures is spent once and is neither facet. The land-fetch half of this facet is the rule below, because a facet rule cannot AND two clauses inside anyOf.
A fetched land taps every turn from then on: the spell resolves once, the acceleration repeats. The same derived `landFetch` as `ramp.landFetchSpell`, so the two cannot drift.
A mana line whose ability `repeats.ts` refused to label, on a card with no labelled engine beside it and no land to fall back on. Shown, not hidden.

REMOVAL THAT COMES BACK (owner, 2026-09-05: 'do the same for removal'). Removal has no effect kind by design, so the ability is found by what it EMITS -- a destroy is a `dies`, an exile or a bounce a `leaves`, a shuffle-into-library a `shuffle`, burn a `non-combat-damage`, -1/-1 counters a `counter-added`, a shrink a `debuff` kind -- and counted as an engine when that ability repeats: an activated kill on a permanent, a 'whenever ... destroy' trigger. Swords is `on-cast` and once; Chupacabra's ETB is once.
A removal ability `repeats.ts` refused to label, with no labelled engine beside it.

A role member whose derived abilities hold no removal-shaped ability at all (no death, leave, shuffle, damage or -1/-1 counter emit, no debuff): the role read it from the printed damage pattern, or from an emit this facet does not list. Nothing to label, so it is said as unlabelled rather than silently read as a one-shot.

NONCOMBAT LIFE REDUCTION OF PLAYERS, read from derived data (#1266; it was the printed `burn` pattern, which needed a digit and missed X damage, "damage equal to", "divided as you choose", drains and upkeep pingers). Damage counts when its subject CAN BE A PLAYER and is not you (`reachesPlayer`: any target, each opponent, a player anyOf like Lava Spike or Pestilence; a creature-only target is removal and has its own rule, "deals 2 damage to you" is a drawback); life loss counts when it is aimed at an opponent or any player, never at you ("you lose 1 life", paying life is a cost); Extort carries its drain only as reminder text, so the keyword is read. A life total SET is not read (derive 367). CEILING: an EMBLEM ultimate lives on its own node (Chandra, Spark Hunter; Karn, Living Legacy; Koth of the Hammer), so the planeswalker is not burn by it. CEILING: an ability GRANTED in quotes to a token or an equipped creature is not the card's own effect and derives none (Mortarpod, Mask of Immolation, Dance with Devils, Devils' Playground, Triskelavus, Dragonbroods' Relic, Sanctum Lurker's planeswalker grant). CEILING: a damage or life-loss clause the model labelled `static` keeps no subject (Duggan, Herald of Hadar, Gonti's Machinations, Chancellor of the Dross), so its effect subject is absent and `reachesPlayer` reads the ability's own damage / life-loss emits instead (Granite Shard, Herald of Hadar read; the redirects Pariah and Palisade Giant, whose emits name a creature or the card, do not). CEILING: a recipient with a relative clause derives a wrong subject (Desolation "each player who sacrificed a Plains" a Plains subtype; Strongarm Tactics "each player who didn't discard a creature card" and Kefka, Dancing Mad a creature/spell type), so those real burn cards are lost. A damage or life-loss REPLACEMENT is no new source and derives no burn kind (a sentence with "instead", a "would ..." frame and the action's own damage / lose word): a redirect onto the card or the enchanted creature's own controller (Treacherous Link, Daughter of Autumn, Ward of Piety, Zhalfirin Crusader), an amplifier (Pyromancer's Gauntlet, Ojer Axonil) and a life-loss or life-gain replacement (Bloodletter of Aclazotz, Tainted Remedy, Plague Drone, Rain of Gore). A redirect whose NEW recipient reaches a player or any target stays burn (Reflect Damage, Eye for an Eye, Harm's Way, Shining Shoal, Captain's Maneuver, Glarecaster, Mirrorwood Treefolk, Megatron's excess damage to the creature's controller): it puts damage on an opponent, and the old role counted it. A damage to the card itself (the fight-back half of Garruk Relentless, Tahngarth, Polukranos) is `self`, and a creature-only anyOf (Sonar Strike, Coward // Killer) is typed by its parent. CEILING: an ability granted in a reminder or a quoted Role (Not Dead After All, Outlaws' Merriment's token).

`forced-sacrifice` is deliberately excluded: the tagger labels edict removal with that kind too, so including it flags Generous Gift as stax. STAX TAXES OTHER PLAYERS (#1530): a tax on the card itself (Strive and "costs more for each target beyond the first": Launch the Fleet, Officious Interrogation; `subject.self`, read per ability) and a tax on the caster's own spells ("Red spells you cast cost {R} more": the Leeches, Geist-Fueled Scarecrow) are drawbacks, not stax. The own-spell tax is read from the printed text, not from the derived subject: the subject is `control: you` for it, but also for Onakke Oathkeeper and Heat Wave ("creatures can't attack planeswalkers you control unless ..."), which tax the opponent, and the subject types (`spell`, `creature`) do not tell them apart. CEILING: the own-spell refusal is card-level, so a card with that line AND a real tax would lose stax (0 today). CEILING: Fireball's "This spell costs {1} more to cast for each target beyond the first" derives a tax with `control: any` and no `self` flag, so it stays stax (a derive defect; the Strive cards derive `self`).

COST REDUCTION IS RAMP (owner 2026-08-06, wired into the rules 2026-10-13, #1190): a Medallion, a Goblin Electromancer, a "second spell costs {2} less" saves the mana a rock would make. The discount must reach OTHER spells (subject scope all/each); a card that only cheapens itself ("This spell costs {1} less", Sunderflock, affinity) is a cheaper card, not ramp (`costNotADiscount`, RULES 22: the derive types Volcanic Salvo's "This spell costs {X} less" with a scope-all subject, and an alternative or free cast -- As Foretold, Aluren, Fires of Invention -- as a reduction; a card whose ONLY such text is that is refused, one that also names a discount for other spells, Hamza, stays). A discount for spells that target the card itself (Spellwild Ouphe, `subject.targets.self`) reaches no other spell: refused (RULES 23). Cost reduction DOES form pairwise edges (it left `ROLE_NOT_SYNERGY` 2026-08-18); tax does not (`ROLE_NOT_SYNERGY` is tax, win-game, extra-turn, extra-phase).

Cultivate/Farseek net +1 land: the derived `landFetch` (#1190; it was two printed-text patterns), which is a fetch ONTO THE BATTLEFIELD from the library. Fetch-to-hand only is card advantage, not ramp.

Putting a land card onto the battlefield from hand (Growth Spiral), from among cards looked at (Planar Genesis) or from a graveyard is an extra land drop, which is ramp (owner ruling 2026-09-27, #512). DERIVED (#1266): an `enters` emit of a land from hand, library, graveyard or exile, whoever the emit control names (Realmbreaker puts a land onto the battlefield under YOUR control and its emit says opp). NOT when the card exiles a land from the battlefield, whoever controls it (Wormfang Newt, Petradon, Realm Razer: a swap or land destruction, not a drop; a CRAFT cost's exile of a Cave is neither, Kaslem's Stonetree keeps it, #1500, Rules 39; Venture Forth exiles from the LIBRARY and stays; Murasa Rootgrazer BOUNCES a land and stays). NOT when the only land search is an opponent's (Old-Growth Dryads, Hired Giant: the derive says the land enters under `any`, which is a defect). NOT when the card destroys, exiles or SACRIFICES all/many lands (Fall of the Thran, Realm Razer; Hew the Entwood, owner 2026-10-17: it sacrifices X lands and puts back at most X, so you never end with more). The derive types "Sacrifice two lands" as the same scope-all `dies`, so this also refuses Planar Engineering, Scapeshift and Natural Balance, and the exile-from-battlefield clause refuses Sowing Mycospawn (its kicked "exile target land"); all four stay Ramp through `landFetch`. CEILING: a card that sacrifices N of its own lands, puts more back, and has NO landFetch would be refused here; 0 such cards today beyond Hew. CEILING: Sacred Ground (retention of a land an opponent destroyed; owner 2026-10-17: NOT ramp) stays IN: its derive carries `ref: trigger` with no trigger object (#1277), so no derived shape tells it from a drop, and matching by name is refused.

A line that makes a mana TOKEN (#1190; it was a printed-text pattern): Treasure/Gold and Eldrazi Spawn/Scion are acceleration. ONE TREASURE BOUGHT BY A SACRIFICE STILL COUNTS (owner ruling 2026-09-27, #534): The Sackville-Bagginses and Ruthless Technomancer, the only two of 419 matching cards whose Treasure waits on sacrificing another permanent, stay ramp -- the Treasure is mana you did not have. Not staple-grade (`rampGrade` 0): a suggestion list offers it only through a synergy.

THE IMPULSE LINE AND THE NET-ZERO SWAPS, READ FROM DERIVED DATA (#1302, owner 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-22). The printed `selection` pattern misses a pick worded "reveal a number of cards ... put one into your hand" (Eye of Yawgmoth), so one card YOU choose from a larger look (`Ability.chooses`, count 1: to-hand, or a typed dig's `toHand`) is read here as well. And a put that nets zero cards is selection, not card advantage: a draw REPLACEMENT (Abundance, Underrealm Lich, Tomorrow, Azami's Familiar, Sages of the Anima) or a SWAP with the top of the library (Scroll Rack) reorders what you will hold (`Ability.netZero`). An opponent's pick (Karn, Scion of Urza) is not YOUR choice and is not here.

SELECTION REORDERS WHAT YOU WILL DRAW; IMPULSE DRAW ADDS CARDS YOU MAY CAST, usually only this turn. The `selection` pattern's third alternative was literally the impulse template, so Light Up the Stage and Jeska's Will were filed as scry. Nearer draw, and carrying a DEADLINE draw does not have, so it is its own leaf rather than folded into either -- inside Consistency, where both neighbours already sit, so the parent count cannot move.

A SPELL ON THE STACK IS ANSWERED BY COUNTERING IT, TAKING IT, REMOVING IT FROM THE STACK, OR REDIRECTING IT, and the answer must be a TARGET (read from derived data since #1266; it was the printed `stack` pattern). Owner rulings 2026-10-14: Commandeer, Invert Polarity, Split Decision, and Mages' Contest by the same shape count. Retargeting your OWN copy is not (#491: derive never reads 'choose new targets for the copy' as a retarget). `control` is deliberately not read: Force of Negation and Defabricate can hit your own spell, and `opp` on a stack emit is a default, not an assertion. WHERE THE 'THAT SPELL' RULE LIVES NOW: a counter, steal or exile of 'that spell' / 'the chosen spell' / 'the spell' carries `scope: target` only when the SAME ability says 'target ... spell' within six sentences earlier -- `targetsASpellEarlier` in derive/emits.ts, with its CEILING (the gap is capped at 6; the corpus maximum is 5, Mages' Contest, on 2026-10-14; re-measure when new cards print). So Kira, Glasskites, Frost Titan and Counterbalance-style untargeted counters, and a cast trigger's own 'exile that spell' (Possibility Storm), stay out. CEILING: redirects that name no TARGET spell are not read by derive: Boltbender ('any number of other spells and/or abilities'), Speedball, New Warrior ('that spell'), Captured by the Consulate ('change the target to enchanted creature'), Psychic Battle ('change the target or targets').

DERIVED (#1266; it was the printed `boardWipe` pattern). A BOARD WIPE IS A MASS EFFECT ON THE BATTLEFIELD: the ability EMITS a destroy, exile or bounce (`dies`, `exiled`, `leaves` from the battlefield) or damage (an ability of kind `damage`) at every creature, permanent, artifact, enchantment, planeswalker or land of ANY controller or the OPPONENTS (`scope` all or each; `control` you is a mass sacrifice or bounce of your own and never counts), a -1/-1 counter on each, or a ONE-SHOT debuff that lowers toughness ("Creatures your opponents control get -2/-2 until end of turn"). Overload is a printed keyword derive does not read, so OVERLOAD plus a targeted kill, damage or toughness debuff of an opponent's or any permanent counts (Cyclonic Rift, Vandalblast, Break the Ice). Owner 2026-11-12: mass land destruction is stax, not a board wipe. The land-only refusal covers every path: the derived kill (`notLandOnly`), the OVERLOAD kill (Break the Ice, Rules 45) and the printed residue (`massOfTargetPlayer` refuses a land-only noun: Ajani Vengeant's "Destroy all lands target player controls", Rules 45). A mass effect whose ONLY subject is lands is NOT a wipe (`notLandOnly`; owner 2026-11-06: mass land destruction is mass land denial, a stax piece, so `stax.landDenial` takes it: Armageddon, Ravages of War, Ruination, Global Ruin, Sunder). A wipe that also hits creatures or other permanents (Jokulhaups, Obliterate, Apocalypse) names another type and stays a wipe. Refused on purpose, each measured on the role-ratchet and pinned by a test: a power-only shrink (Cumber Stone, -1/-0) and a CONTINUOUS shrink (Kaervek, Elesh Norn: a hoser, not a sweep) (`oneShotToughnessDebuff`); an edict forced on one named player (`notEdict`: Dead Drop); an OPPONENT's kill whose ability carries a plain number, or whose subject is a COUNTED pick (`notCountedOppKill`: Portal to Phyrexia, Crackling Doom, Soul Shatter; "two permanents", Bane of Bala Ged; "that many", Phyrexian Obliterator, Ravenous Rotbelly; a sacrifice by every player, or with no number, keeps its role: Barter in Blood, Cataclysm, Pox), EXCEPT a printed "sacrifices half" (owner 2026-11-09, #1581: a half-of-the-board sacrifice is a wipe in practice, like Pox: Vona's Hunger, Rakdos the Defiler; derive stores half as a counted pick with no amount, so the printed words are the cue; CEILING: a card printing "sacrifices half" beside a separate "that many" is not told apart); a mass that widens ONE TARGET ("exile target nonland permanent and all other ... with the same name": Banishment, Echoing Ruin, Hubris; `notBesideTargetedKill`); the Auras and Equipment attached to a TARGET (`notAttachedTo`: Blastfire Bolt; a global "Destroy all Auras" stays, Serene Heart, Pure // Simple); token-only masses on both the kill and the debuff path (`notTokenOnly`: Faerie Artisans, Bloodline Culling, Aether Snap); a block's result (`notBlockCombat`, on kill, damage and debuff: Alaborn Zealot, Plague Wight, Gomazoa); a fight (the damage emit of a kind-less ability); a mass about the card itself; a subject that is only planeswalkers (`typeAny`: Kumano Faces Kakkazan). A wipe takes precedence over targeted removal, so the rule `removal.targeted` refuses what this one takes (`rule` op). PRINTED RESIDUE (the one `oracle` op left here): derive scopes "all creatures TARGET PLAYER controls" as `target`, the same shape as "destroy target creature", so `massOfTargetPlayer` reads the printed text, and needs a permanent noun before "controls" for damage (Mogg Infestation, Rain of Daggers, Primeval Light, Settle the Wreckage, River's Rebuke, Aggravate, Simoon; Typhoon and Treacherous Terrain burn a player and stay out). CEILING: derive misses, each a real wipe the old pattern had and this rule has not: Genesis of the Daleks chapter IV (the model stored the whole villainous choice as ONE object, and the destroy inside it is not read); a STATIC "All creatures get -1/-1" (Night of Souls' Betrayal) is a continuous shrink; Spring Cleaning's conditional mass sits in the same clause as its target (`notBesideTargetedKill` refuses it). Fixed by derive 466 (#1549): "of the creature type / color of your choice" no longer reads as control `you` (Extinction, Wash Out, Root Greevil, Space Beleren, Witch's Vengeance), "power greater than the number of cards in your hand" is a count (Nightmare Unmaking), "power greater than target creature's power" is not one target (Fell the Mighty), and "except for lands and tokens" no longer names the class (Elspeth Tirel, Scourglass). CEILING: derive over-reads, each a card this rule has and main's pattern had not, none guarded: a trigger-less ability beside the block trigger (Venom, Venomous Fangs, Infinite Authority), Corrosive Ooze (an attachment sweep with no sibling target), Aura Barbs, Archfiend of Spite, Avacyn's Judgment ("divided among any number of targets"), Blow Your House Down ("up to three target creatures"), Summon: Valefor (an opponent chooses one creature, `each`), Tunnel of Love, Prowling Pangolin ("any player may sacrifice"; Worms of the Earth had the same and is no wipe since the land-only refusal), Dispense Justice (its second ability lacks the edict flag), Giant Albatross, Master of the Wild Hunt (wolves deal damage), Graf Rats (a meld). Fixed by derive 466 (#1549): Godsend, Haphazard Bombardment and Zurgo and Ojutai ("one of those"), Mega Flare ("each of the chosen creatures"), Missy (the dealer's sentence read as the recipient), Xathrid Demon ("a creature other than this creature"). Remaining ones filed as derive issue #1549. Measured by role-ratchet over the commander-legal corpus (2026-11-06, derive 465): the oracle-op count in rules.json fell from 28 to 27. Derive 466 (#1549), role-ratchet: boardWipe gained 7 (Elspeth Tirel, Extinction, Fell the Mighty, Nightmare Unmaking, Root Greevil, Space Beleren, Wash Out) and lost 7 false ones (Godsend, Haphazard Bombardment, Mega Flare, Missy, Oracle en-Vec, Xathrid Demon, Zurgo and Ojutai).

DERIVED (#1266): the ability EMITS a kill, exile, shuffle or bounce of an opponent's or any permanent that it targets (a `dies`; an `exiled`, `leaves` or `shuffle` from the battlefield, refusing an immediate flicker of your own permanent), a -1/-1 counter on a target, a debuff that lowers toughness, or a forced sacrifice, or an EDICT (a `dies` marked `edict`: "target player sacrifices a creature of their choice" targets the player and no creature, #1295; it replaced the printed `targetPlayerSacrifices` pattern); plus TARGETED DAMAGE whose allowed target includes a permanent (`reachesPermanent`, #1294; it was the printed `damageRemoval`). Owner ruling 2026-10-22: "any target", "target creature", "target creature or planeswalker", a battle, and "target player or planeswalker" (through the planeswalker: Lava Spike) are removal at ANY amount, a 1-damage ping and a repeatable pinger (Prodigal Pyromancer) included; "target player" / "target opponent" (derive 381 marks them `player`), "each opponent" and a creature you control are burn or nothing. A damage REDIRECT ("the next 2 damage ... is dealt to any target instead": Harm's Way, Glarecaster; derive 382 marks it `redirect`) and damage the victim may have dealt (Requiem Monolith, `victimMay`) are not removal (owner ruling 2026-10-22); prevent-then-deal (Refraction Trap) deals damage and stays. NO GRAVEYARD-HATE GUARD (#1326): the printed `graveyardHate` pattern (`exile ... graveyard` anywhere in the text) was a `not` here and refused 85 cards with real removal whose graveyard exile is a cost, an escape / embalm / encore / craft / delve line, or a SECOND mode (Grim Lavamancer, Phlage, Magmatic Sinkhole, Harvest Pyre, Cleanup Crew, Rakdos Charm). It guarded nothing: the removal clauses read derived emits, and an exile out of a graveyard derives `fromZone: graveyard`, which the exile clause (`fromZone: battlefield or none`) does not accept, so pure graveyard hate (Bojuka Bog, Relic of Progenitus, Scavenging Ooze) never matched. Measured with the guard deleted: 85 cards gained, 0 lost, all real removal, none graveyard hate. DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE: the answer classes `damage` / `damage.any` keep their own #581 meaning (2+ damage for "any target"), so a 1-damage ping fills this role and answers no class. An emit the victim may decline (`victimMay`: "its controller may sacrifice it", "unless that player sacrifices it") and a permanent "you own" are not removal. A wipe takes precedence, so a mass effect is not counted in both. That was an else-if in code and is a `not` clause here. A destroy whose controller gets copies back is not removal (owner ruling 2026-09-27, #513: Saw in Half is played on your own creatures to win or combo).

AN AURA THAT STRIPS A PERMANENT IS REMOVAL (issue #566): Frogify, Lignify, Kenrith's Transformation, Imprisoned in the Moon -- the creature stays and does nothing, which players count as removal. 'Enchanted creature/permanent loses all abilities' or 'is a colorless land'. 26 commander-legal Auras (2026-09-27).
The classes are the Aura's ENCHANT line: Imprisoned in the Moon answers a creature, land or planeswalker; Stop Cold an artifact or creature.

A KEYWORD HANDED TO SOMETHING ELSE IS PROTECTION; ONE THE CARD KEEPS FOR ITSELF IS A STAT (roadmap I1: a creature with hexproof protects itself, not the board). DERIVED (#1266; it was the printed pattern `hexproof|indestructible|protection from|can't be countered|shroud|phases? out` and a text reader of who the sentence was about). Five readings, any one: (1) a GRANT of hexproof, indestructible, shroud or protection (`Ability.grants`) whose recipient is not the card itself (`Ability.grantsSelf`, derive 515; or the grant's own `subject.self`: Chromium, the Mutable, Gideon, Champion of Justice): Heroic Intervention, Lightning Greaves, Mother of Runes, Avacyn, 'You have hexproof' (Leyline of Sanctity), a quoted grant to others (Agent of the Shadow Thieves). 'This creature gains indestructible' (Adanto Vanguard), 'Dragonlord Ojutai has hexproof as long as it's untapped' and the same fact behind a condition or a trigger ('As long as you control four or more artifacts, this creature has hexproof': Shimmer Dragon; 'Landfall -- ..., this creature gains indestructible': Dreadwurm) are the card's own. A printed keyword derives no grant (Sylvan Caryatid), nor does a token made 'with hexproof' (Deeproot Waters: the token's, owner ruling 2026-09-27 #533), 'lose hexproof' (Shadowspear, Hour of Devastation), a keyword list the card counts (Akroma, Vision of Ixidor) or a name that holds the word (Skyshroud Sentinel). (2) a KEYWORD COUNTER (hexproof, indestructible, shroud) put on a permanent that is not the card: Claim the Kingdom, Slippery Bogbonder, Summon: Knights of Round. 'Enters with an indestructible counter on it' (the Myojin) and 'Put an indestructible counter on Drivnod' are the card's own and are refused (`notSelf`, and the `enters-with-counters` kind is not read). (3) a `phases-out` EMIT whose subject is neither the card itself nor an opponent's permanent: Teferi's Protection, Slip Out the Back, Clever Concealment; a phase-out of ANY permanent, yours or theirs, can be protection and interaction both (Galadriel's Dismissal). Owner 2026-11-12: Dream Fighter is opponent-aimed and leaves Protection: 'this creature and that creature phase out' fires when it blocks or becomes blocked by a creature, and 'that creature' is the one blocking it or blocked by it, which an opponent controls (CR 509.1a); derive reads that referent `control: any`, so the rule refuses a phase-out only a block triggers (`notBlockCombat`) rather than the derive reading changing for every block trigger (Engulfing Slagwurm, Inferno Elemental ...). Owner 2026-11-12: a card that protects only itself is not Protection, phasing included (Blink Dog, Mist Dragon, Vaporous Djinn, Kaito Shizuki: 11 cards leave). Owner 2026-11-12: phasing aimed only at an opponent's permanent is interaction, not Protection (Divine Smite, Sapphire Charm, Teferi's Reproach, Teferi, Master of Time, Teferi, Timeless Voyager). Owner 2026-11-12: a land can carry Protection, so the `countsAsLand` exclusion is gone (Sejiri Steppe, Tower of the Magistrate, Plaza of Heroes, Tyrite Sanctum, Cavern of Souls, Boseiju, Mistrise Village; the spells of a land-faced modal card too: Emeria's Call, Revitalizing Repast, Sejiri Shelter). Talon Gates of Madara ('up to one target creature phases out') joins: its stored clause files the phase-out as a `put` action, and derive 518 reads a zoneless `put` in a clause that prints 'phases out' and no put as the phase-out (`phaseOutFiledAsPut`). Detection Tower ('creatures your opponents control with hexproof can be the targets of spells and abilities you control as though they didn't have hexproof') is anti-protection and stays out: derive 519 reads 'as though they didn't have <keyword>' as naming the keyword, never granting it (Kaya, Bane of the Dead and Nowhere to Run store `cant` and never granted). CEILING, misses: Oubliette's stored clause holds only the tap of its second sentence ('Tap that creature as it phases in this way'), so it derives no phase-out; The War Doctor only counts permanents that phase out. (4) ONE PRINTED RESIDUE, `protectionUnread`. CEILING: derive has no reading of 'can't be countered' handed to other spells (Delighted Halfling, Vexing Shusher, Allosaurus Shepherd, Rhythm of the Wild, Destiny Spinner; 'This spell can't be countered' is the card's own and is not matched) and none of protection for the PLAYER written 'you gain protection from' / 'You have shroud' (The One Ring, Seht's Tiger, Solitary Confinement, Noble Heritage; derive files the first two as lifegain), so those 33 cards stand on printed text. A new effect kind is vocabulary work beyond this role. CEILING, misses: an EMBLEM's grant lives on the emblem's own node (the Venser CEILING in rules.ts), so Domri Rade, Elspeth, Knight-Errant, Nissa, Who Shakes the World, Oko, Lorwyn Liege and Vivien Reid lose the role; 'Choose hexproof or indestructible. Creatures you control gain that ability' names no keyword in `grants` (Linvala, Shield of Sea Gate); a per-colour keyword list derives no grant (Scion of Draco); a keyword named in a mode's bullet derives none ('gains that ability. • 1/3 Turtle with hexproof': Wild Shape); 'target creature phases out until this enchantment leaves' derives no emit (Oubliette). CEILING, over-reads: Celebr-8000's 'it gains the indicated ability' is a sentence away from the bullet that names indestructible, so `grantsSelf` is not set; Kaito, Bane of Nightmares' 'he's a 3/4 Ninja creature and has hexproof', Opal Guardian's 'becomes a 3/4 Gargoyle creature with flying and protection from red' (the card animating itself, with a keyword: derive writes the keyword as a grant and `grantsSelf` reads only a 'gains / has' sentence whose subject is the card) and Blitzwing's 'gains that ability' (a random pick of flying or indestructible, no keyword on the sentence) are read as protection; the keywords of an ANIMATE ride as a grant when derive writes one (Sylvan Awakening's lands 'become 2/2 Elemental creatures with reach, indestructible, and haste' count; Avalanche Caller's 'becomes a 4/4 Elemental creature with hexproof' derives none and does not). (5) a TARGETING BAN THAT PROTECTS SOMETHING OF YOURS, from any source (owner 2026-11-12, twice): the derived `targeting-ban` kind (`banProtects`). Against opponents first: `targetingBan.source.control: opp`, 'can't be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control' (Vines of Vastwood, Canopy Cover, Shielding Plax, Veilstone Amulet, Display of Dominance's blue-and-black spells, Tomik's lands and land cards in graveyards; Display of Dominance and Tomik confirmed Protection, owner 2026-11-12). Then a ban from ANY source, when it covers your things: a subject that is yours (Autumn's Veil and Spellbane Centaur, 'creatures you control can't be the targets of blue ... spells'; Autumn's Veil prints no 'opponents'), an AURA's enchanted creature, which is one you can put on your own creature (Anti-Magic Aura, Spectral Shield, Artifact Ward), a global ban on every graveyard (Ground Seal, Silent Gravestone, Dennick, Pious Apprentice, Underworld Cerberus) or on every creature (Dense Foliage). The card's own ban is hexproof on itself and is refused whatever the source (`notSelf`: Thrun, Breaker of Silence; Shanna, Sisay's Legacy; Karplusan Strider; Gaea's Revenge; Raiding Party; Bartel Runeaxe), and so is a ban whose subject is only opponents' things. Peace Talks ('players and permanents can't be the targets of spells or activated abilities', this turn and next) does NOT join: its subject is every permanent and player, not graveyards or creatures; NEEDS RULING whether a global ban on all permanents counts.

A FLICKER IS PROTECTION (owner ruling 2026-09-25). Exiling your own permanent and returning it makes a new object (CR 400.7), so the removal aimed at it loses its target (CR 608.2b). Only at instant speed -- an instant, or a card with flash -- since protection has to answer a spell on the stack; Flicker (a sorcery), Flickerwisp and Brago cannot. DERIVED (#1266; it was three printed patterns): a `flicker` ability whose subject is not an opponent's permanent (that is a blink, not a shield: Banisher Priest's shape derives `control: opp`), and not the card itself (Nezahal exiles and returns only Nezahal), on an Instant or a card that prints the Flash keyword. No instant or flash card in the corpus (derive 515) derives either refused shape; both are pinned on written rows. The printed patterns needed 'exile target' and 'return it / that card', so they missed Ghostway ('each creature you control'), Eerie Interlude and Semester's End ('any number of target ... Return those cards'), Displace, Ghostly Flicker and Illusionist's Stratagem ('up to two target ... those cards'), Cosmic Intervention (a replacement), Silver Surfer, Cosmic Voyager and the X-target instants. ACTIVATED FLICKER, owner 2026-11-12: an ACTIVATED flicker is at instant speed too, so it is Protection on a permanent of ANY card type with no flash (Eldrazi Displacer, Mistmeadow Witch, Roon of the Hidden Realm, Emiel the Blessed, Abuelo, Nephalia Smuggler, Cold Storage, Synod Sanctum; also Angel of Condemnation, Baboon Spirit, Distinguished Conjurer, Elrond, Gilraen, Niko, Triad of Fates, Voyager Staff, Touch the Spirit Realm's Channel, Ruin Ghost, and the lands Endless Sands and Northampton Farm). It still refuses a flicker of only the card itself and of only opponents' permanents, and a flicker of 'another target creature' of any controller counts (it can be interaction too). Derive also types 'put a card exiled with this onto the battlefield' as `flicker` (Karn Liberated, Ashiok, Sisters of Stone Death, Ghost Vacuum, Profane Procession) and a loyalty or sorcery-speed exile-and-return (Aminatou, Venser, Kaya, The Eternal Wanderer, Lilysplash Mentor) as one, so the activated branch reads `pairedInstantExile`: an instant-speed exile of a permanent that is not the card itself, and a return to its OWNER or an exile of YOUR permanent. A planeswalker's loyalty ability and 'activate only as a sorcery' are sorcery speed and stay out. CEILING: the pair is read across the whole card, not the clause (Cold Storage exiles in one ability and returns in another). Livio, Oathsworn Sentinel joins on 'Its controller may exile it with an aegis counter' and the return of every aegis card to its owner (Protection: owner 2026-11-12). CEILING, over-reads: Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd has flash but flickers on ATTACK (the keyword is read off the card, not tied to the flickering ability; so was the printed `flashKeyword`); Audacious Swap's 'If it's a land card, they put it onto the battlefield' derives as a one-branch return (`returnIf`, the misread named in rules.ts), and `returnIf` is not refused because Parting Gust and Vindictive Triumph are real.

A PRINTED SEARCH OF YOUR OWN LIBRARY IS A TUTOR; A TYPED DIG IS NOT (owner ruling 2026-10-21). DERIVED (#1266): a `search` ability with `librarySearch: yours` (Demonic Tutor, Rhystic Tutor, 'your library and/or graveyard', 'graveyard, hand, and/or library': Finale of Devastation, Boonweaver Giant, the 'card named X' planeswalker-deck cards). Not another player's search (Sphinx Ambassador, Path to Exile), and not a reveal-until or look-at-the-top dig (Commune with Nature, Hermit Druid, Winota), which derive also types as `search` for edges but leaves without `librarySearch`. A search whose subject is land only is fixing, not a tutor (Farseek, Expedition Map, Pir's Whim's land search); a subject with no type is not land-only. The keyword tutors derive does not read are read off the printed keyword list: Transmute, Transfigure, and Typecycling unless the card is Landcycling (Plainscycling, basic landcycling and artifact landcycling fetch lands or a fixed artifact: Sojourner's Companion leaves the role). CEILING: an EMBLEM ultimate's search lives on the emblem's own node (same accepted gap as the Venser CEILING in rules.ts), so Garruk, Unleashed; Garruk, Caller of Beasts; Kaito Shizuki and Tezzeret, Artifice Master lose the role. CEILING: a land-only fetch beside a non-land mode keeps the role through that mode (Aang's Journey's Shrine, Analyze the Pollen and Traverse the Ulvenwald's creature-or-land, Verdant Crescendo's named card).

A REVEAL-UNTIL-A-NAMED-CARD IS A TUTOR (owner 2026-10-22): Demonic Consultation, Divining Witch and Spoils of the Vault name a card and reveal until it turns up, which finds that card as surely as a search does, with no printed "search" (so `tutor.text`'s `librarySearch` cannot see it). DERIVED: `Ability.named` (derive 385). NOT "put all of them with the chosen name into your hand" (Desperate Research, Tamiyo, Wood Sage), which may find nothing: that is hand-fill.

Owner 2026-11-12: mass land destruction is stax, not a board wipe. MASS LAND DENIAL IS STAX (owner 2026-11-06: mass land destruction is mass land denial, a stax piece, not a board wipe). The ability EMITS a destroy, exile, sacrifice or bounce (`dies`, `exiled`, `leaves` from the battlefield) at every land, or every land of a kind ("nonbasic lands", "all Forests"), of any controller or the opponents (`scope` all or each; `control` you is a mass bounce of your own and never counts): Armageddon, Ravages of War, Ruination, Global Ruin, Sunder, Natural Balance, Planar Overlay, Omen of Fire. It reads the same derived emits as `boardWipe.text`, which refuses a land-only subject. A single land destruction (Stone Rain: scope target) is neither. A WIPE THAT ALSO DESTROYS LANDS IS BOTH a `boardWipe` and stax (owner 2026-11-06, #1554): the land can be its own emit (Wildfire, Death Cloud, Pox, Destructive Force, Devastating Dreams, Restore Balance, Decree of Annihilation's cycling trigger) or part of a combined type list (`includesLand`: "artifacts, creatures, and lands" in Jokulhaups, Obliterate, Decree of Annihilation) (Devastation, Catastrophe, Soulscour). ALL PERMANENTS IS BOTH (#1557, Rules 41): a genuinely unrestricted `permanent` names lands (`includesLand`): Apocalypse, Worldfire, Dimensional Breach. Derive 468 keeps the restriction of the permanent subjects that used to look the same (`chosenColor`: Wash Out; `colorCount`: All Is Dust; `selection`: all-but Razia's Purification and Mount Doom, votes Council's Judgment, pile Liliana of the Veil, attached-to End Hostilities), and those do not count. A per-opponent choice is no mass (Ultimate Magic: Meteor: "for each opponent, choose an artifact or land ... destroy the chosen permanents", `selection: chosen`, no scope), so it is not stax; it stays a wipe by its 7 damage to each creature. CEILING: a restriction derive does not read still files an unrestricted `permanent` and counts. There is no `boardWipe.text` refusal any more. Type-keyed land destruction (Acid Rain, Boil, Tsunami, Flashfires, Stench of Evil) stays stax, as shipped. OVERLOAD (Rules 45): a land-only target kill plus the printed Overload keyword is a mass (Break the Ice, "each" for "target"), so it is stax. CEILING: Ajani Vengeant's "Destroy all lands target player controls" derives scope target, so this rule cannot tell it from Stone Rain; it is stax only through its other abilities (stax.text), not through its mass land destruction.

GRAVEYARD HATE IS CARDS EXILED FROM A GRAVEYARD THAT IS NOT YOURS, OR A REPLACEMENT THAT EXILES CARDS BOUND FOR ONE (design 12.3; DERIVED since #1266, it was the printed `graveyardHatePositive` pattern). Promoted from a negative filter on removal to a category of its own: `graveyardHate` (the broad pattern `exile...graveyard`) stays only as the veto removal rules use, where an over-match costs one missed removal count. As a positive category the printed pattern was wrong on two thirds of what it caught (delve, encore, escape and craft costs, self-recursion all say 'exile ... graveyard' about YOUR OWN yard) and blind to static hate (Rest in Peace says 'graveyard' before 'exile'). Now: an `exiled` emit from a graveyard (`fromZone: graveyard`) that is not owned by you and not the card itself (Bojuka Bog, Decompose's 'a single graveyard', Honor the Fallen, Planar Void, Cemetery cards), OR a `graveyard-hate` effect over an opponent's or any graveyard with no owner you (the replacements: Leyline of the Void, Valgavoth, Dauthi Voidwalker, Rest in Peace, Sanctifier en-Vec, Dryad Militant, Anafenza; CR 614.6: the replaced event never happens, so the card never reaches the graveyard and derive emits exiled and no leave). NOT hate: a FORCED exile is hate whoever's yard (Augusta, Curse of Oblivion, Mudhole, Graveyard Shovel, Burn Away) but one the VICTIM CHOOSES is not (`victimMay`: Carrion Rats, Carrion Wurm, Grave Consequences, Lost in Thought, Axebane Ferox's tax, Gravestorm, Web of Inertia; the precedent is the edict's `notVictimMay` in removal); exiling a card from a graveyard that is not yours COUNTS even when the card is then used (Gruesome Encore, Saruman, Soundwave, Narset, Reenact the Crime, Foggy Swamp Visions, The End, the Scarab God shape: it still leaves their yard); a dies or sacrifice trigger of YOURS exiling the card (Promise of Tomorrow, the Rectors, Nightmare Shepherd) is your yard, an opponent's (Mari, Patron of the Vein, Shelob: it exiles every opposing creature that dies; the processor ability puts cards INTO a graveyard and derives nothing) or any player's (Planar Void, Mimic Vat, Koh, Whippoorwill) is not. NOT hate: your own yard (delve, escape, Necropotence, Bag of Holding, Purgatory; derive marks the emit `owner: you`; Living Death, Living End and Scrap Mastery are each player's OWN yard coming back), the card exiling itself from your graveyard (renew, channel-like costs), the spell riders of #1306 ('If that spell would be put into a graveyard, exile it instead' exiles a spell from the STACK: Kess, Impulsivity), and the PROCESSORS that put a card from exile INTO a graveyard (Mind Raker, Ulamog's Reclaimer, Wasteland Strangler, Ruin Processor, Murk Strider, Void Attendant, Oracle of Dust, Processor Assault, Cryptic Cruiser, Memory Theft). An exile naming a graveyard in a trailing hand/graveyard list (Identity Crisis, Thought Distortion, Ashiok's -10) and a search-and-exile over 'graveyard, hand, and library' (Surgical Extraction, Cranial Extraction, Slaughter Games, Lost Legacy, Eradicate, The End, Pick the Brain) are one exiled emit per zone named (#1311). CEILING: an exile naming a graveyard beside the battlefield keeps the model's single zone or none (Ultimate Nullification, Angel of Serenity); Crabomination (the grammar reads 'library, graveyard, and hand' as library, hand, hand); Samurai of the Pale Curtain (a permanents-only replacement, unread by derive); Diabolic Servitude (the creature it put onto the battlefield dies: derive cannot say whose graveyard, so it reads as any); the GRAMMAR path zones Savior of Ollenbock and Silent Gravestone wrongly (#1309).

Equipment, creature-enchanting Auras and cards that act as one, DERIVED since #1315 (it was the printed `voltronAura` pattern). An Aura counts when it can enchant a creature (`characteristics.enchants` names creature or permanent, control not opp) and it HELPS the creature it enchants (#574): a host pump that raises power or toughness, a host keyword or speed grant, host evasion, a QUOTED ability that is no curse, regenerate, umbra or totem armor, or an Aura that can only enchant your own creature. A card that is NOT an Aura by subtype but attaches (bestow creatures, Licids, Cloudform / Lightform / Rageform) counts on a host pump, grant or evasion alone. Refused when it hurts or takes the creature: goad, gains-control, a host ability-loss, a host restriction that forbids ATTACKING (Pacifism, Arrest, Utopia Vow, Pillory of the Sleepless, Compulsory Rest), a defender or phasing grant, or a host debuff with no host pump in the same clause. Owner rulings 2026-10-22: (1) an either-or Aura (Clutch of Undeath +3/+3 as a Zombie, otherwise -3/-3; Mishra's Domination, otherwise it can't block) stays voltron, and a block-only restriction is no negative; (2) a conditional buff (the Demigod, Deity and Oversoul cycles, Rune of X, Favor of Jukai) IS voltron; (3) 'judge the quote': a keyword-grant with empty `grants` counts when derive wrote at least one ability for the quote (`grantedBy`) and none is a curse (a sacrifice or death of the grantee or of a permanent you control, a life loss or damage aimed at the grantee or its controller). The curse check only stops a quote from counting as the POSITIVE: an Aura with another positive (a pump, evasion: Shifting Shadow, Crystalline Nautilus) stays voltron, as on main. A sacrifice in a granted ability's COST counts as a curse (Minimus Containment's Treasure is refused). CEILING (#1315, derive 374): (1) a quote with NO child ability is not judged and not counted: Bewitching Leechcraft and Oblivion Crown are lost against the printed pattern (and the Talent cycle, In Bolas's Clutches, Unable to Scream, Fog on the Barrow-Downs, Psychic Overload, Ghoulflesh never counted). (2) `enchants` is unset for 'Enchant creature or Vehicle' (Aerial Modification, Siege Modification, Silken Strength, Lightwheel Enhancements, Roadside Assistance) and for Dance of the Dead (a card in a graveyard): those Auras are missed. (3) Derive reads nothing for Awesome Presence and Dog Umbra (a conditional umbra armor), and Aspect of Wolf's pump has no sign: lost. (4) Canopy Cover and Artifact Ward carry a spurious ability-loss (their 'can't be the target'): lost. (5) Predatory Urge's quote hurts the grantee and is refused. A keyword grant that is a drawback other than defender or phasing reads as a help.
A creature bigger than it costs, with no token channel -- design 12.5's 'stat predicate on power vs MV, no token or anthem channel'. A token producer that happens to be a beater is go-wide first.

Same derived signal the `burn` build category uses (`burn.effect`, read from derive since #1266, with its CEILINGs: emblem ultimates, granted abilities, model-`static` clauses with no subject). Damage aimed at a creature is removal and has its own rules; this is the half that can reach a player. The effect must not be aimed at you (#574): The Chain Veil's 'you lose 2 life' is `player-life-loss` too, and read as a burn plan on Chandra.

MILL AIMED AT AN OPPONENT OR AT ANY PLAYER (DERIVED since #1266, it was the printed `millOpponents` pattern). Self-mill is fuel, not a wincon, and the same effect text serves both: a `mill` EMIT of an opponent or any player (the printed pattern wanted the player named before 'mills' and missed 'that player mills' (Anowon, Crosstown Courier, Shriekgeist), 'its controller mills' (Countermand, Psychic Strike, Grisly Spectacle), 'defending player mills' (Nemesis of Reason), 'any number of target players each mill' (Riverchurn Monument)). NOT a mill: the graveyard half of a DIG ('put the rest into your graveyard': Fact or Fiction, Hermit Druid, Animal Magnetism; derive reads it as a mill with the player any and the cards `fromZone: library`, which a real mill never carries); MANIFEST DREAD (its mill emit sits under a kind-less ability: Manifest Dread, Fear of Impostors, Killer's Mask), checked on the same ability by `abilityKind`; and since derive 368 an EXILE of the top of a library is an exile, not a mill (CR 701.17a: Sire of Stagnation, Black Widow, Lidless Gaze, Plargg and Nassari, Possibility Storm, Ulamog; the own-library impulse cards fed 'enters your graveyard' payoffs as self-mill). CEILING: Jace, Vryn's Prodigy (its mill is the -9 emblem's, which lives on the emblem's own node); the reveal-until mills (Mind Grind: 'each opponent reveals cards from the top of their library until ... puts all cards revealed this way into their graveyard') derive `fromZone: library` like a dig and are not read, as the printed pattern missed them too; Ulamog, the Ceaseless Hunger now reads as an exile and is no mill plan though it empties a library; Chains of Mephistopheles (each player's incidental one-card mill) counts as any player's.

A STATED WIN OR LOSS CONDITION, DERIVED since #1266 (it was the printed `altWin` pattern): the `win-game` effect kind (CR 104.2b: Epic Struggle, Thassa's Oracle, Laboratory Maniac, Simic Ascendancy, Hellkite Tyrant, Revel in Riches; derive 368 reads the clause verb, 1 card derived it before) or a `loses-game` emit of an opponent or any player (Phage, Atemsis, Vorpal Sword, Triskaidekaphobia). YOUR OWN LOSS IS NEVER A PAYOFF (owner ruling 2026-10-16, #1252): a self 'you lose the game' (Phyrexian Pacts' upkeep, Lich's Mastery leaving, Phage's cast clause, Immortal Coil) emits `loses-game` of `control: you` and does not count; a card that prints both keeps the opponent's. Every derived `win-game` is `you`, unstated, or `any` (Celestial Convergence's symmetric win, Twenty-Toed Toad, Biovisionary); never an opponent's, so the rule keeps no control filter on it. No longer matched, the printed pattern's false positives: the poison reminder text '(A player with ten or more poison counters loses the game.)' (15 cards: Crypt Cobra, Marsh Viper, Pit Scorpion, Virulent Sliver, Snake Cult Initiation ...), and a REACTION to someone's loss ('Whenever a player loses the game': Blood Tyrant, Elbrus, Sengir, Share the Spoils, Curse of Vengeance). Not a win condition: 'can't lose the game' / 'can't win the game' (Platinum Angel, Everybody Lives!) and a replacement of your own loss (The Golden Throne) derive none. CEILING: Vraska, Golgari Queen (the -9 emblem's 'that player loses the game' lives on the emblem's own node, as Jace, Vryn's Prodigy's mill does); the loss of a player a trigger or 'the chosen player' names (Zenos yae Galvus // Shinryu) keeps whatever control derive read; a win printed inside a clause the model files under another verb is not read (the census over the commander-legal cards: 40 print a win sentence, 39 derive win-game, the residue is Everybody Lives!'s prohibition).

DERIVED (#1266; it was the printed `damageRemoval` pattern). Burn answers what it can hit: Flame Slash answers a creature, Broadside Barrage a creature and a planeswalker. The card has a `damage` effect that TARGETS (`reachesPermanent`: a typed non-player subject, the targeted emit where an energy cost left the effect subject-less: Aethertorch Renegade, Dynavolt Tower) a creature or planeswalker of an opponent or any player, at ANY amount (owner 2026-10-22, as `removal.targeted`): a 1-damage ping at a named creature (Elite Javelineer) counts, a 1-damage ping at "any target" does not (`answers.damage.any`). Not a damage REDIRECT or one the victim may decline. The class is the type the subject names (`reachesClass`): a type list, an `anyOf` branch, or an unrestricted `permanent`; a subtype alone names none, and a compound noun (`allTypes`: "artifact creature", Electrostatic Bolt, Gremlin Mine) is a creature. The PLANESWALKER class additionally refuses a subject that can be a player (`notReachesPlayer`): main read only "target creature or planeswalker" and never "target player or planeswalker" (Lava Spike) or "opponent, creature or planeswalker". Measured over the commander-legal corpus against the printed pattern (rule alone, creature class): 490 to 866 cards, +383 -7; planeswalker 65 to 150, +85 -0. GAINED, a genuine fix: damage that is not a digit (X, "equal to its power", "the number of lands you control": Heat Ray, Earth Tremor), a bite ("target creature you control deals damage equal to its power to another target creature": Contest of Claws), "divided among" and "each of two target creatures" (Forked Lightning, Swelter), "up to one target", "another target" and "attacking or blocking" between the verb and the type (Ben-Ben, Harpoon Sniper), and "target creature, planeswalker, or battle" (Volcanic Spite). LOST, a genuine fix: damage to a creature YOU control (Rile, Spiteful Bully, Whiptail Moloch: the printed class could not see "you control"), "target player ... and each creature that player controls" (Chandra's Flame Wave, Urabrask // The Great Work), "target opponent for each creature card" (Lotleth Giant). NEEDS RULING: a COLOUR HOSER is a creature answer here, as on main (Combust "5 damage to target white or blue creature", Rending Volley, Fry, Essence Burn): the printed class captured only the word "creature", so `COLOUR_HOSER` never saw the colour. The other answer rules drop a colour (`notColourLocked`); damage keeps main's reading until the owner rules. "Target player or planeswalker" (Lava Spike, 3 damage) answers no planeswalker, as on main; reading it would add about 170 cards to answer:planeswalker. CEILING: real misses. Coward // Killer (a subject whose scope sits in `anyOf` branches), the two damage emblems and a token's quoted "deals 3 damage to any target" (Chandra, Spark Hunter, Koth, Dragonbroods' Relic: an emblem and a token are their own nodes). CEILING: over-read. a damage clause beside a stored condition ("if that land is a Mountain, this creature deals 2 damage instead": Akoum Hellkite) reads the instead-amount.
As answers.damage.creature, for the planeswalker class: `notReachesPlayer` keeps main's reading ("creature or planeswalker", "planeswalker"; never "player or planeswalker").

DERIVED (#1266; it was the printed `damageRemovalAny` pattern). Lightning Bolt says "any target", which is a creature or a planeswalker (or a player) (issue #581, owner 2026-09-26): a `damage` effect that TARGETS an UNTYPED non-player subject (`untyped`) of an opponent or any player. Two damage or more, or a damage that is no printed number (X, "its power", "that much"): a 1-damage ping from Goblin Bombardment or Prodigal Pyromancer is not what a player means by an answer (`amountAtLeast`). A separate rule rather than a wider `answers.damage`, which names its type. Measured against the printed pattern (rule alone): 425 to 605 cards, +187 -7. GAINED, a genuine fix: damage with no printed digit ("damage equal to its power to any target", X) and "deals 2 damage to any OTHER target" (Bond of Passion: `any other target` was no key of the class table, so the card matched the pattern and gave no class), "each of two targets" (Furious Reprisal, Pinnacle of Rage). LOST, a genuine fix: an EMBLEM's or a token's quoted damage (Chandra, Spark Hunter; Koth, Fire of Resistance; Dragonbroods' Relic) and "target player or planeswalker" at 1 (Chandra, Dressed to Kill). CEILING: none known.
As answers.damage.any.creature, for the planeswalker class ("any target" reaches both).

DERIVED (#1266; it was the printed `tuckRemoval` pattern). Chaos Warp shuffles any permanent into its owner's library and Condemn puts a creature on the bottom (issue #581). A `shuffle` emit, or a `leaves` emit marked `tuck` (a put into a library from the battlefield), of an opponent's or any player's permanent the card TARGETS (battlefield or no stated zone), whose subject can be the class (`reachesClass`: "nonenchantment permanent" and "noncreature permanent" name their classes by what they are not, and a card from a graveyard is no permanent on the battlefield). Refused: a colour hoser (`notColourLocked`), your own permanent (`notOwnedByYou`) and one the victim may decline. Measured against the printed pattern (rule alone): creature 59 to 94 (+39 -4), artifact 31 to 51 (+22 -2), enchantment 28 to 43 (+17 -2), planeswalker 21 to 38 (+18 -1), land 11 to 13 (+2 -0). GAINED, a genuine fix: the "owner puts it on their choice of the top or bottom of their library" template (Dire Downdraft, Misleading Motes, Vanish from Sight), "its owner shuffles it" (Deglamer, Blink), "two target lands on top of their owners' libraries" (Plow Under), and shuffles of the card itself plus a target (Void Stalker, Floodpits Drowner). A tuck that is one branch of an else (Consign to Dream, Rona's Vortex: "if kicked, put it on the bottom instead") counts. LOST, a genuine fix: a card in a graveyard (Keeper of the Cadence: "target artifact, instant, or sorcery card from a graveyard"), and the class a card names by what it is not (Audacious Swap's enchantment, Brutalizer Exarch's and Primal Command's creature). CEILING: real misses. Lashweed Lurker (derive reads "its owner's library" as control `you`), Proteus Staff (the polymorph family is read as played on your own creature, owner ruling 2026-10-02, #962).
As answers.tuck.creature, for the artifact class.
As answers.tuck.creature, for the enchantment class.
As answers.tuck.creature, for the planeswalker class.
As answers.tuck.creature, for the land class.

DERIVED (#1266; it was the printed `shrinkRemoval` pattern). 'Target creature gets -3/-3' kills most creatures and is removal to `targeted removal`; Nowhere to Run, Tragic Slip and Vilis answered nothing (issue #581). A `debuff` effect that TARGETS a creature of an opponent or any player and lowers toughness (`toughnessDown`: -2/-0 shrinks an attacker and kills nothing), not the losing side of a coin flip (Orcish Captain) and not a colour hoser. Measured against the printed pattern (rule alone): 262 to 266 cards, +5 -1. GAINED, a genuine fix: a qualified type between `target` and `creature` (Toxic Stench "target nonblack creature") and a shrink per energy or per land (Die Young, Drown in Filth). LOST, a genuine fix: a token's quoted "target creature gets -1/-1" (Skirk Ridge Exhumer, #533). CEILING: marks. the NARROW mark (a stat or state condition on the target) is read only on the printed-text path, so a derived rule carries none: Skulking Killer ("if that opponent controls no other creatures") now counts whole. The same holds for Barrin's Unmaking, Nimbus Champion and Sage-Eye Avengers in `answers.bounce`.

DERIVED (#1266; it was the printed `counterShrinkRemoval` pattern). A -1/-1 counter on a target creature, repeated (Yawgmoth), is creature removal to `targeted removal` and was none here (issue #581): a `counter-added` emit of a -1/-1 counter on an opponent's or any player's creature the card TARGETS, not a colour hoser. Measured against the printed pattern (rule alone): 57 to 56 cards, +7 -8. LOST, a genuine fix: a -1/-1 counter on a creature YOU control, the cost of a creature with an enters-with-counters drawback (Baleful Ammit, Channeler Initiate, Crocodile of the Crossing, Plague Belcher: the printed class could not see "you control"). GAINED, a genuine fix: "each of up to two target creatures" and "distribute" (Grind // Dust, Splendid Agony, The Reaper, King No More), "roll X dice" (Attempted Murder) and the counter after a damage clause (Puncture Bolt). Contagion Engine ("each creature target player controls", which derive scopes as one target) is a mass -1/-1 and counts. CEILING: none known.

DERIVED (#1266; it was the printed `bounceRemoval` pattern). A bounce is a weaker answer than a kill -- it answers the board, not the card -- but it is an answer, and `targetedRemoval` has always counted it. A `bounce` effect that TARGETS a permanent of an opponent or any player whose subject can be the class (`reachesClass`: "nonland permanent" is not a land; a card in a graveyard, a spell, and a bare subtype such as "Aura" name no class), not a permanent you own and not a colour hoser. Measured against the printed pattern (rule alone): creature 230 to 321 (+100 -9), artifact 102 to 140 (+40 -2), enchantment 101 to 137 (+38 -2), planeswalker 98 to 134 (+37 -1), land 43 to 42 (+4 -5). GAINED, a genuine fix: a counted or optional object that is not `return target` ("return up to two target creatures", "return X target creatures", "return another target nonland permanent", "return six target nonland permanents": Aether Tide, Captivating Gyre, Aether Gale, Disruptor of Currents). LOST, a genuine fix: RECURSION from a graveyard ("return target creature card from a graveyard to its owner's hand": Disturbing Plot, Revive the Fallen, Pulse of Murasa, Vampire Charmseeker: the printed class read "creature card from a graveyard" as creature), and a token-only or Aura-only subject. CEILING: real misses. Crystal Shard ("unless its controller pays {1}" derives a bounce with no subject), Seedling Charm and a bare subtype ("target Aura" names no class), and "target spell or permanent", which derive reads as the permanent SPELL intersection and so without land (Venser, Shaper Savant; Divide by Zero; Jeskai Revelation lose their land class). CEILING: over-reads. Getaway Car ("target creature that crewed it" is yours), Alchemist's Retrieval ("nonland permanent [you control]"). CEILING: marks. see `answers.shrink`.
As answers.bounce.creature, for the artifact class.
As answers.bounce.creature, for the enchantment class.
As answers.bounce.creature, for the planeswalker class.
As answers.bounce.creature, for the land class.

The same enumeration `targetedRemoval` already carries, captured instead of collapsed to a boolean. Answer classes are a SEPARATE axis from build categories: a card is in both, and this rule deliberately does not exclude board wipes, because a wipe does answer creatures.

`typedRemoval` is `(?:destroy|exile)` -- one alternation, so nothing downstream can tell a recursion-proof answer from one a reanimator undoes. This rule ADDS to `answers.typed` rather than replacing it: every exile removal matches both, once for the class and once for the mode, so no card changes class. The first `not` is the same veto `answers.typed` carries, and it is load-bearing here: 'Exile target creature card from a graveyard' names a creature and answers nothing on the battlefield. The second `not` is only on THIS rule, never on `answers.typed`: a blink (Long Road Home, Flicker, Venser's +2) exiles and then RETURNS the permanent, which is the least recursion-proof answer there is -- worse than a destroy, since the threat is back on a timer the opponent doesn't even have to work for. Measured on the corpus: 114 cards match `exileRemoval` and a return-to-battlefield clause; they stay in `count` (`answers.typed` has no such veto, by design) and simply carry no `exile` mark.

OWNER 2026-11-12: PHASING OUT ANOTHER PLAYER'S PERMANENT IS INTERACTION, BUT NOT REMOVAL. It answers the board for a turn, as a bounce does, so it carries an ANSWER class by what the phase-out can hit and is deliberately in no build category (`removal.targeted` reads kills, exiles, shuffles, -1/-1 counters, toughness debuffs, forced sacrifices and damage, never `phases-out`, so the role does not move). DERIVED: a `phases-out` emit whose subject is an opponent's or any player's permanent that the card TARGETS (Teferi's Reproach 'all nonland permanents they control' is a target opponent's: creature, artifact, enchantment, planeswalker; Sapphire Charm, Teferi, Master of Time and Teferi, Timeless Voyager: creature; Divine Smite: creature and planeswalker, and its 'If that permanent is black, exile it instead' is the exile emit that keeps its targetedRemoval). `permanent` expands to every class. Refused: the card itself (Blink Dog), a permanent you control (Teferi's Protection, Clever Concealment), and a phase-out only a BLOCK triggers (Dream Fighter, `notBlockCombat`). A phase-out of a target of ANY controller counts, because it can hit an opponent's (Galadriel's Dismissal, Slip Out the Back, Brokers Confluence): a card that is mainly protection keeps its answer class too (owner 2026-11-12: Slip Out the Back and Galadriel's Dismissal confirmed). A TARGETLESS MASS phase-out (`scope: all`) of creatures, by an emit of an opponent's or ANY controller's permanents, answers creature and is NOT a board wipe (owner 2026-11-12: Out of Time, Time and Tide, Disciple of Caelus Nin; The City on the Edge of Forever's 'all artifacts and creatures' answers creature and artifact), so `boardWipe` is not added. The mass branch reads the types the emit names, NOT the `permanent` expansion: Teferi's Realm ('chooses artifact, creature, land, or non-Aura enchantment ... all nontoken permanents of that type phase out', derived as type `permanent` with a chosen kind) gets no class, because the chosen type is unread; NEEDS RULING. A mass phase-out of only YOUR permanents has `control: you` and is refused (Teferi's Protection, Perch Protection, Ripples of Potential, Taniwha, Temporal Firestorm). CEILING: Disciple of Caelus Nin's 'all permanents other than this creature' derives with type `creature`, so it answers creature only, not every class.
As answers.phaseOut.creature, for the artifact class (a `permanent` subject reaches every class).
As answers.phaseOut.creature, for the enchantment class (a `permanent` subject reaches every class).
As answers.phaseOut.creature, for the planeswalker class (a `permanent` subject reaches every class).
As answers.phaseOut.creature, for the land class (a `permanent` subject reaches every class).

Graveyard hate is the one answer class §12.3 says does not score on count: one Bojuka Bog answers a recursion engine not at all, Rest in Peace answers it forever. Deliberately carries NO `category`, so the `graveyardHate` build category keeps its own rule and its own count and cannot move. Read off oracle text rather than off `Ability.repeats`, which is the right data on the wrong subject -- answer detection matches the CARD, so nothing links a repeatable label to the ability that does the answering. The activated-ability alternation's determiner is narrowed to `(?:a|an opponent's|that|their)` -- the same allow-list `graveyardHatePositive` already uses -- because an unrestricted 'exile ... graveyard' after a `{cost}:` caught Lazotep Quarry, whose activated ability exiles from ITS OWN graveyard to reanimate a copy. Self-reference is the largest defect family this engine has had (74% of all false edges, project history); widening this determiner back out re-admits it. The static-prohibition alternation is narrowed to `can't (?:enter|be cast|be played)` -- a prohibition must name WHAT it prohibits, or it is not hate at all. Unconstrained, 'cards? in graveyards? can't' corpus-wide catches two unrelated failures: cards with no graveyard interaction at all (Demoralize, Exquisite Firecraft, Gilded Cerodon -- a threshold/spell-mastery/desert template that happens to contain the phrase) and the SIGN INVERTED -- 'cards in graveyards can't be the targets of spells or abilities' (Ground Seal, Underworld Cerberus, Dennick) is graveyard PROTECTION, the thing a graveyard deck runs to stop hate, not hate itself. Measured on the corpus: the unnarrowed pattern adds 15 cards to `answer:graveyard` that `graveyardHatePositive` does not already cover; 8 of the 15 are wrong (6 named above plus Silent Gravestone and Tomik, both caught the same sign-inverted way) and none of the 8 appears in the 71 calibration decks, so the population gate could not see this. Narrowed, 7 corpus-wide additions remain, all real: Grafdigger's Cage, Kunoros, Soulless Jailer, Weathered Runestone (the four already in the 71 decks) plus Ashes of the Abhorrent, Graveyard Shovel and Merrow Bonegnawer outside them.
